solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Kinky sex put finally aside — a lot protest

indicators.note: kinky means twisted or bent, so the letters around it are bent into a new order
finally points to the closing letter only of the word it qualifies

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of aside
taken as written

explanation.surface: A disapproving onlooker sets aside the racy behaviour and objects loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: To expostulate is to argue earnestly against something, a verb synonym for protest.

clue.text: Stretch of river crowded with vessels

indicators.note: a place crowded with things is filled by them, so they go inside

blocks.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
pans are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: A stretch of river busy with boats.
explanation.walkthrough: Vessels suggests ships on the river; here they are kitchen pans.
explanation.definitionFit: An expanse is a wide open area, a large stretch of land, sea or sky.

clue.text: Be taken for a backward clod, wearing clothing in pieces

indicators.note: backward tells us the word for clod is read bottom to top
the clothing of a word is its outside, its first and last letters
one who is wearing something has it wrapped round them

blocks.note: taken as written
an ass is a fool, a clod
the outside letters of pieces

explanation.surface: A dim oaf dressed in rags is mistaken for someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass as something is to be accepted or taken for it, a phrasal verb synonym.

clue.text: Batty old rector's interminable bad language

indicators.note: batty means crazy, so the letters are scrambled
interminable is read as without a terminal, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then its last letter goes

explanation.surface: An eccentric elderly vicar never stops swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad language' reads as swearing, but language alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Serbo-Croat is the South Slavic tongue spoken in the former Yugoslavia.

clue.text: Vital substance about to overwhelm Uganda's interior

indicators.note: to overwhelm a place is to overrun and take it over, so one piece displaces another
interior marks the inner letters of the word as the part being displaced

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
taken as written; its inside letters are replaced

explanation.surface: An essential substance is about to swamp central Uganda.
explanation.definitionFit: Urea is a compound produced by living bodies, a vital substance in the sense of belonging to life.

clue.text: Hormone with equal parts of hydrogen and nitrogen

blocks.note: and means with or plus

blocks.clueFragment: equal parts of hydrogen and nitrogen
blocks.note: the identical closing part that both gas names share

explanation.surface: A hormone made from equal parts of two gases, like a chemistry recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: Hydrogen and nitrogen both end in the same five letters; that shared part is the equal part of each.
explanation.definitionFit: An androgen is a male sex hormone such as testosterone.

clue.text: Retired author cycled around tree in green

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so in a down answer the word is read upwards
cycled around means letters move round from the end of the word to its front

blocks.note: the author of the clue refers to the setter as me
the alder is a tree

explanation.surface: A retired writer goes cycling round a tree in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The final two letters of the tree name are rotated round to its front.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerald is a vivid shade of green, named after the gemstone.

clue.text: I get rid of point of sale — stopping stags?

indicators.note: something stopping a gap plugs it, so this piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: stags are male deer
POS is the retail abbreviation for point of sale

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a shop till blocking a herd of stags.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the answer's own voice: a deposer could say 'I get rid of' rulers.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposer removes a ruler from office, so the noun can introduce itself as the one who removes.

clue.text: Evolution of very naked apes led to men?

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its outer covering, so only the inner letters stay
evolution means change over time, so the letters develop into a new order

blocks.note: v is the abbreviation for very
the inner letters of apes
taken as written

explanation.surface: A quip on human evolution: hairless apes gave rise to people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evolution' does double duty, as the definition and as the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Evolution is the gradual growth of something into a more advanced form, which is development.

clue.text: Like Billy No-Mates, wasting half a day out of bounds

indicators.note: wasting something means losing it, so these letters drop out of the word

blocks.note: Billy No-Mates is British slang for a person with no friends
the first half of FRIDAY

explanation.surface: A lonely person drifts about, losing half a day somewhere forbidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of bounds' looks like 'forbidden', but here it means outside all limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Something endless has no limits at all, so it lies beyond every boundary.

clue.text: Talent wasted snorting pot

indicators.note: wasted means drunk or stoned, so the letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's gift goes to waste because they are taking drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong point is a quality someone excels at, much like a talent or forte.

clue.text: Spicy stuff John served with French wine and dhal every now and then

indicators.note: now and then means at intervals, so only every other letter is kept
a dish served with others sits alongside them, so these parts are placed side by side

blocks.note: vin is French for wine
the first and third letters of dhal
john is slang for a toilet, as is loo

explanation.surface: John is served wine and the odd spoonful of lentil curry.
explanation.definitionFit: Vindaloo is a fiery hot curry, so it counts as spicy food.

clue.text: Nonsense books secured by locks

indicators.note: a thing secured by another is held in its grip, so it goes inside

blocks.note: locks of hair
OT, the Old Testament books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Volumes fastened with padlocks are dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot air is an idiom for empty talk with no substance, just like nonsense.

clue.text: Transported — so tore new bra off!

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so these letters are spoilt into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Carried away with passion, someone rips off a new bra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transported' suggests ecstasy; the definition means carried by water.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterborne goods are carried on ships, so they are transported by sea or river.

clue.text: 'Place to rest,' you said

indicators.note: said tells us we want the word as spoken, not as written

blocks.note: to lie down is to rest
the letter U is pronounced the same as you

explanation.surface: Someone tells a friend where to lie down for a rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieu means place, mostly in the idiom 'in lieu of', meaning in place of.

clue.text: Old fellow attached to division securing battlefield

indicators.note: attached to means joined on next to, so these parts stand side by side

blocks.note: an arm is a division or branch of an organisation
aged means old
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A veteran soldier joins an army division that captures a battleground.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is read back to front: the division comes first, then the old fellow attached after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Armageddon is the biblical site of the final battle between good and evil, hence a battlefield.

clue.text: Retired, constrained by very little money? That's make-believe

indicators.note: constrained by means held in on all sides, so this piece sits inside

blocks.note: pence are the smallest British coins
ret is the abbreviation for retired

explanation.surface: A pensioner short of cash wonders whether the money is real.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretence is pretending, the acting out of things that are not real, which is make-believe.

clue.text: Deadpan Rod overturned coffee

indicators.note: overturned in an across answer means turned back to front

blocks.note: a poker is a metal rod for stirring a fire
decaf is decaffeinated coffee

explanation.surface: Rod knocks over his coffee and keeps a straight face about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod reads like a man's name but is the fireside tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker-faced means showing no expression, which is what deadpan describes.

clue.text: Starkest relative's inherently predatory character

indicators.note: inherently means within by nature, so the answer lies inside the words

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A grim relative has a predatory nature at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Character suggests a person's nature, but here it means a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A kestrel is a small falcon, a bird of prey that hunts small animals.

clue.text: Check work on the way

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing on another simply comes after it

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Checking a job done on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to halt or restrain it, a verb synonym for stop.

clue.text: A student visiting different parts of old German city for advertisement

indicators.note: visitors go inside a place, and here two pieces enter it at separate points

blocks.note: Trier, founded by the Romans, is among Germany's oldest cities
taken as written
L for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A student touring an old German city is used in a promotional campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A trailer is a short preview promoting a film, so it serves as an advertisement.

clue.text: Able lady from city avoiding extremes

indicators.note: avoiding the extremes means leaving off each word's ends and keeping the middles

blocks.note: the inner letters of lady
the inner letters of from
the inner letters of city

explanation.surface: A capable urban woman who keeps away from extremes.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady, from and city look like a description; each word just gives up its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and clever, an adjective synonym for able.

clue.text: Bogus king once posed by entrance to zoo

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: ER, Edwardus Rex, for a former King Edward
to sit for a portrait is to pose
the first letter of zoo

explanation.surface: A fake monarch poses for photos at the zoo gates.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior imitation or substitute, so it means fake or bogus.

clue.text: American practice needing time to absorb friend's capital

indicators.note: needing here means lacking, so that letter goes missing
something that absorbs another takes it inside itself

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
a habit is a regular practice
T is the abbreviation for time
bud is American slang for a friend

explanation.surface: An American routine that needs time to welcome a pal into the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The American and the shortened practice together wrap round the friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Abu Dhabi is the capital city of the United Arab Emirates.

clue.text: Measure of force feed delivered

indicators.note: delivered as in a speech delivered, so we want the word as spoken

blocks.note: to dine is to feed

explanation.surface: A measured amount of food is brought by delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' suggests a takeaway arriving; here it means spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: The dyne is the unit of force in the old centimetre-gram-second system.

clue.text: Radio consumes variable unlimited power

indicators.note: what consumes something swallows it, so the other piece goes inside

blocks.note: tranny is old British slang for a transistor radio
y is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A broadcaster swallows up every changing thing with boundless power.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyranny is cruel, absolute rule, power held without any check.

clue.text: Two heartless men reversed lease for minor part of plant

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is cut away
reversed tells us to read the combined letters backwards

blocks.note: taken as written, then its middle letter goes
OR, other ranks, is crossword shorthand for soldiers or men
to let a property is to lease it

explanation.surface: Two soldiers back out of a rental agreement over some garden shoots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two heartless' is not about men without hearts: it is the word two losing its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rootlet is a small subsidiary root, a minor part of a plant.

clue.text: Editor tipped select novel, being a dedicated monitor of fiction

indicators.note: tipped means having its tip taken off, so the first letter is lost
novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then its first letter goes

explanation.surface: A publisher's editor picks a new book, being devoted to fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel and fiction both pretend to be about books; the fiction monitored here is lies.
explanation.definitionFit: A polygraph detects untruths, so it is a machine devoted to spotting made-up stories.
